title: Escape a heavier planet
hook: Change central mass and predict escape speed.
misconception: escape speed doubles when central mass doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply v_escape = √(2GM/r) to compare escape speed when central mass changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a Newtonian spherical body with fixed launch radius and no other gravitating bodies, v_escape = √(2GM/r). When central mass doubles, escape speed becomes √2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model v_escape = √(2GM/r); scaling exponent 0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a Newtonian spherical body with fixed launch radius and no other gravitating bodies, with a nonzero initial result. If central mass triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on escape speed?
recall.why: Apply v_escape = √(2GM/r) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is √3.
